notes: §1985:VI.6.27.3 SR2: "Identifier-1, identifier-2, identifier-3, and identifier-5 must reference data items described, implicitly or explicitly, as category alphanumeric." BindUnstring asks UnstringSenderCategory of the sender and of every DELIMITED BY operand and Sr2OffendingCategory of the DELIMITER IN item; the predicate IsAlphanumericOrNational admits an alphanumeric group and an elementary item of category alphanumeric or national and nothing else, and Reject reports COBOL1651. There is no edition arm; the national half is unreachable at 85, where national data is refused at its declaration (COBOL0900). Probed at --std 85: a numeric DISPLAY (the witness), numeric-edited, alphanumeric-edited and alphabetic sender, a numeric, COMP, numeric-edited and alphabetic delimiter (first, after OR and under ALL) and a numeric, alphanumeric-edited and alphabetic DELIMITER IN item are refused; an alphanumeric item (also JUSTIFIED), a group in each of the three positions and a reference-modified numeric item as delimiter (category alphanumeric by §1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5) are accepted, and a numeric identifier-4, which the rule does not name, is accepted.

next.reason: 1985 VI.6.27.3 SR2: identifiers 1, 2, 3 and 5 'must reference data items described ... as category alphanumeric'. §2023:14.9.48.3 SR2: they 'shall reference data items of category alphanumeric or national', and §2023:14.9.48.3 SR3 requires all operands national if any is. Every conforming 1985 UNSTRING is still accepted with the same meaning, but 2023 accepts national operands the 1985 rule refuses: a compile-time relaxation, no exception condition.
